text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Italian president Oscar Luigi Scalfaro criticised the European Central Bank and the German Bundesbank for keeping on judging Italy's likelihood to join EMU in schedule by 1999, repeating that the country is asking for no special treatment or discounts (all).

* Hard-left Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti defined the government as "seeking adventure", repeating his party is ready to withdraw its support and head for new elections. Bertinotti criticised Prime Minister Romano Prodi's "opening" towards opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi, who told reporters an agreement between the majority and the opposition over financial measures to help Italy into the single European currency would be "useful" but very unlikely to happen (all).

* Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar is reportedly quoted as refusing Prodi's proposal for a "Latin agreement" between Spain, Italy and France. Aznar repeated that each country must see to fulfill Maastricht Treaty requirements (all).

* Italian statistic office Istat confirmed that inflation fell to 2.4 percent year-on-year in February from 2.6 percent in January. According to Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi the falling trend for inflation should continue (all).
* Ciampi said "in his opinion" the mini-budget measures for 1997 will not be less than 14 trillion lire (all).

* Ciampi said the share exchange ratio for the merger of state telecoms holding Stet and telephone operator Telecom Italia will be revealed in the next few weeks. Ciampi also confirmed the planned fusioni of Telecom Italia into Stet will be completed by June and added that the decision on the possible use of a golden share for the sale of telecoms holding Stet is up to the government and not to the group's board (all).
* Ciampi also said state industrial holding Iri should sell its stake in Banca di Roma (Sole 24 Ore).
* Italian new car registration in February rose some 20 percent over February 1995 with Fiat group marques seeing sales up 23 to 25 percent, according to Fiat Auto MD Roberto Testore (all).
* The dollar rose above 1,700 against the lira (all).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
